security_audit.summary: The Markdown examples and most filesystem patterns are safe documentation or normal temporary file handling. The script intentionally runs Lighthouse and accepts an arbitrary URL, which creates a network reachability risk in agent environments.

remediation.issue: Unrestricted URL input can make Lighthouse fetch internal or sensitive network targets.
remediation.suggestion: Validate schemes, block localhost and private IP ranges, and require explicit user approval before auditing a URL.

remediation.issue: Temporary Lighthouse reports may remain if the subprocess times out or fails before cleanup.
remediation.suggestion: Move temp file deletion into a finally block and delete partial reports on every exit path.

remediation.issue: The script resolves the lighthouse executable from PATH.
remediation.suggestion: Document the expected Lighthouse installation and avoid running the script in directories or environments with untrusted PATH entries.

finding_verdicts.reason: subprocess.run invokes a fixed lighthouse command with a list of arguments and shell execution is not enabled. The user-provided URL is passed as a single argument, so I did not find command injection evidence.
The hardcoded URL is only an example in the script usage docstring. It is not contacted by the script unless a user supplies it at runtime.
This line only imports the tempfile module. The import is expected for Lighthouse output handling and is not a filesystem operation by itself.
The script creates a temporary JSON report with delete=False and only removes it after successful parsing. A timeout or early failure could leave a report file in the temp directory.
os.unlink is used to delete the temporary Lighthouse report after it is read. This is cleanup of a file created by the same script, not destructive user file access.
The backticks are Markdown inline code formatting around a usage example. They are not Ruby or shell backtick execution.
This location begins a Markdown fenced code block that documents a profiling workflow. It contains no executable shell command or backtick substitution.
The URL appears inside a documented command example for running the audit script. It is not a hidden endpoint or automatic network destination.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted URL Auditing
semantic_findings.description: The Lighthouse script accepts a URL argument and passes it to Lighthouse for fetching. In an agent environment, this could be used to reach localhost, private networks, or metadata services unless guarded by policy.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script takes sys.argv[1] and uses it as the Lighthouse target URL. This is intended behavior, but no validation or private-network guard is present.

content.value_statement: Slow applications are hard to improve without reliable measurements. This skill guides profiling workflows and Lighthouse audits to identify practical optimization targets.
actual_capabilities: Explains Core Web Vitals targets for loading, interactivity, and visual stability.
Provides a four-step workflow for measuring, identifying, fixing, and validating bottlenecks.
Maps common performance problems to Lighthouse, bundle analyzers, and browser DevTools.
Runs a Lighthouse audit script against a supplied URL when the CLI is installed.
Summarizes Lighthouse category scores for performance, accessibility, best practices, and SEO.
limitations: The audit script requires the Lighthouse CLI to be installed separately.
Results depend on network conditions, hardware, and browser environment.
The skill identifies likely bottlenecks but does not automatically rewrite application code.
The script can only audit URLs reachable from the current execution environment.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Performance Baseline
use_cases.description: Measure current page speed before starting an optimization project.

use_cases.title: Review Release Readiness
use_cases.description: Check Core Web Vitals and Lighthouse categories before shipping a web change.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Optimization Work
use_cases.description: Translate slow page symptoms into focused actions for product planning.

prompt_templates.title: Explain My Scores
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a Lighthouse result.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the performance-profiling skill to explain my Lighthouse scores in plain language and list the first three fixes to try.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Profiling Tools
prompt_templates.scenario: Selecting the right tool for a symptom.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the performance-profiling skill to match these symptoms to the best profiling tools: slow load, delayed clicks, memory growth, and scroll jank.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Optimization Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the performance-profiling skill to create a prioritized plan for improving a web app with slow initial load and large JavaScript bundles.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Release Candidate
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the performance-profiling skill to run or review a Lighthouse audit for my release URL, then identify risks, tradeoffs, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: A dashboard has slow first load and a large main bundle.
output: Measure a baseline with Lighthouse and browser performance tools.
Inspect bundle size for large dependencies, duplicate packages, and missing route splits.
Prioritize code splitting, dependency trimming, compression, and image optimization.

output_examples.input: A page feels delayed when users click filters.
output: Profile the interaction in DevTools Performance.
Look for long tasks, heavy event handlers, layout work, and unnecessary rendering.
Fix the largest blocking task first and validate the interaction again.

output_examples.input: A Lighthouse run shows acceptable SEO but poor performance.
output_examples.output: Focus on loading metrics first. Check render blocking resources, image size, unused JavaScript, cache headers, and compression before changing SEO content.

best_practices: Measure a baseline before changing code.
Fix the largest verified bottleneck before smaller issues.
Validate improvements with the same tool and comparable conditions.
anti_patterns: Do not optimize based only on guesses or visual impressions.
Do not chase micro-optimizations before fixing major load and runtime issues.
Do not rely only on lab data when real user monitoring is available.

faq.question: Does this skill run Lighthouse automatically?
faq.answer: It includes a Lighthouse audit script, but the Lighthouse CLI must be installed and available.

faq.question: Can it improve Core Web Vitals?
faq.answer: It helps identify actions that can improve LCP, INP, and CLS, but it does not edit application code.

faq.question: Which tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Lighthouse, Lighthouse CI, bundle analyzers, browser performance tools, memory tools, and network inspection.

faq.question: Can I use it in CI?
faq.answer: The guidance supports CI workflows, but the included script is a local helper and may need wrapping for CI.

faq.question: What input should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide a URL, Lighthouse results, symptoms, bundle details, or profiling observations.

faq.question: Does it need network access?
faq.answer: The guidance does not need network access, but the Lighthouse script fetches the URL being audited.
